title: ICM Lesson Card v1
description: The output contract for the lesson-card.v1 profile. Every field below is REQUIRED and appears in every card in the order declared by `fieldOrder`, regardless of what the input contained. A field with nothing in the source carries the literal string `not in source`. Every leaf value taken from the input is a `quote` object carrying the verbatim text and the byte span it was cut from.
minimumCoveragePctNote: A SEPARATE, AGGREGATE gate on top of unmappedThresholdBytes. unmappedThresholdBytes only catches a single CONTIGUOUS uncovered run at or above 32 bytes; it does not catch loss spread across many runs each individually under that bar. This value is the loosest floor that clears every shipped card (cards/*.json: 97.97-99.10%) and fixtures/control/card.json (86.79%) with real headroom, while still catching a card that has silently shed a double-digit percentage of its input in small pieces (measured: trimming every claim in a shipped card by ~20 bytes at word boundaries drops 14.8% of the input and recomputes to 83.28%, below this floor). It is a floor, not a guarantee: a card that loses content in scattered runs that still sum to LESS than this percentage is not caught by either gate. See coverage's own description for the exact combined claim.

absent.description: The one and only absent-value marker. Never null, never an empty string, never an empty array, never an omitted key.

span.description: A half-open byte range [start, end) into the UTF-8 bytes of the file named by source.file. Byte offsets, not character offsets and not line numbers: the inputs this profile accepts are single-line transcripts, where a line number locates nothing.

quote.description: Verbatim text cut from the input, plus the span it was cut from. The invariant the verifier enforces: bytes(source.file)[span.start:span.end] decoded as UTF-8 is byte-identical to `text`. No trimming, no case folding, no whitespace collapsing, no spelling normalisation.

listOrAbsent.description: A populated array, or the absent marker. NEVER an empty array — `[]` is ambiguous between 'the input had none' and 'the converter did not look', and this contract does not permit that ambiguity.

schema.description: Identifies this contract. A reader who has this string can open this file and check the card against it.

profile.description: The conversion profile that produced the card. The engine is profile-agnostic; this names which contract was selected.

generated_utc.description: Wall clock at generation, read from the system at write time. File metadata about the card, NOT a claim extracted from the input.

source.description: Identifies the exact bytes every span in this card points into. file/sha256/bytes/duration_seconds are metadata ABOUT the input file, not claims extracted FROM it — the transcript does not state its own hash. duration_seconds comes from the transcription metadata shipped in inputs/PROVENANCE.md, and is `not in source` when no such metadata exists.

file.description: Path to the input, relative to the repo root. This file ships in the repo so every span is re-checkable. The verifier constrains this beyond the bare string type: it must resolve strictly inside the repo (no absolute path, no `..` traversal — SOURCE_FILE_ESCAPES_REPO), it must sit under `inputs/` or `fixtures/` (the only two directories this profile treats as holding citable transcript bytes — SOURCE_FILE_NOT_ALLOWED), and an `inputs/` path must be one of the files listed in `inputs/sha256sums.txt` (SOURCE_FILE_UNREGISTERED). A card whose own filename matches one of the registered inputs' basenames (e.g. a file living at `cards/04-pricing-objection.card.json`) is additionally bound to cite exactly that input (SOURCE_FILE_IDENTITY_MISMATCH), so a shipped card cannot be repointed at a different, uncontrolled file while keeping its name. This does NOT prove the named file is the CORRECT source for a card verified under an unrelated name or path — a card verified from outside that naming convention may still cite any real file under `fixtures/`, which is a disclosed residual gap, not a hidden one.

sha256.description: sha256 of the input file. If this does not match the shipped bytes, every span in the card is void and the verifier fails before checking anything else.

duration_seconds.description: Media duration in seconds, from the transcription metadata shipped in inputs/meta.json (summarised for humans in inputs/PROVENANCE.md), keyed by the input's basename. `not in source` when meta.json has no entry for this input. Sibling metadata, not a claim extracted from the transcript's own text — but it is NOT merely asserted: the verifier re-reads inputs/meta.json itself and checks this field against it exactly, so a fabricated or stale value fails with SOURCE_DURATION_MISMATCH.

title.description: A title stated IN the input, verbatim. Never composed, never borrowed from the filename, never borrowed from a video's published title — if the speaker did not say it, this is `not in source`.

name.description: The speaker's name EXACTLY as it appeared in the input. Never normalised to the usual spelling. If the transcript renders a name the way dictation heard it, the card carries what the transcript said.

evidence.description: The span of the phrase that established the speaker, e.g. a self-introduction. A name with no establishing phrase is not a speaker.

claims.description: Assertions the input makes, each verbatim with its span.

definition.description: The definition AS GIVEN in the input. Not a better definition, not a corrected one.

value.description: The figure verbatim, including any currency symbol, separators and spelling as they appeared. `$5,000` is not `5000`.

unit.description: The unit AS STATED, span-backed. A unit the input did not state is `not in source` — units are the easiest place to smuggle an invention in.

numbers.description: A number with no span cannot ship. This is the field where a single drifted digit loses the comp, so it is fully span-backed.

name.description: Spelled as it appeared in the input. Never corrected.

kind.description: A SCHEMA CLASSIFICATION, not a claim extracted from the input. It is only ever set to something other than `unknown` when the input itself states the role, in which case `role` carries that span. This field is the one place the card holds a label rather than a quote, and it is deliberately fenced: no role span means `unknown`.

role.description: The span where the input stated what this entity is. `not in source` forces kind to `unknown`.

index.description: 1-based position in the procedure. Must increase by exactly 1 across the array.

steps.description: The ordered procedure, only if one was stated. Step spans must be strictly increasing in `start`: a procedure is narrated in order, so a step whose span jumps backwards is pointing at a repeat of the same words somewhere else in the input. That is the neighbour attack, and the verifier rejects it even though the bytes match.

reason.description: Why the schema had nowhere to put it. A closed enum, so this stays a lookup rather than a paragraph of prose the reader has to trust.

unmapped.description: What the schema could not hold. The verifier RECOMPUTES this set from the source rather than trusting the card: any stretch of input not covered by some span, above the declared threshold, must appear here. Two independent, recomputed gates enforce this, and NEITHER is a general guarantee that nothing important disappeared: (1) unmappedThresholdBytes — no single CONTIGUOUS uncovered run may be at or above 32 bytes; (2) minimumCoveragePct — total covered bytes across the whole card may not fall below the profile's aggregate floor (see that top-level keyword), which exists precisely because (1) alone permits the same total loss spread across many runs each individually under 32 bytes. A dropped passage at or above the 32-byte bar, OR a combined loss that pushes total coverage below the aggregate floor, fails the card. Loss that stays under BOTH bars is, by construction, undetectable — that is a stated limit, not an oversight.

coverage.description: How much of the input the card accounts for. Fully recomputable from the spans, and the verifier recomputes it — a card cannot assert a coverage number its own spans do not support.

unmapped_threshold_bytes.description: The lesson-card.v1 profile's fixed omission bar (see the top-level `unmappedThresholdBytes` keyword on this schema), restated here so a reader can see it without opening the schema. This is NOT a bar the card sets for itself: the verifier reads the real bar out of the schema, uses that for the omission scan regardless of what this field says, and separately checks that this field equals it — a card that stated a different number here fails with COVERAGE_THRESHOLD_NOT_PROFILE. A card cannot exempt itself from the omission gate by inflating this number.
